speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle and are now presenting with increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with episodes of pain during urination. To understand the connection between these symptoms, have you noticed any redness, warmth, or fever associated with your current knee pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your sexual history and the triad of arthritis, urethritis (pain with urination), and a recent self-resolving joint issue, I suspect reactive arthritis. Are you currently experiencing eye pain, redness, or sensitivity to light?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (formerly Reiter's Syndrome)
